_comment: Hand-curated corrections for upstream OpenSkiMap clustering artifacts.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
OpenSkiMap clusters runs and lifts into ski areas geometrically. Where two
separately-marketed resorts share lift-linked terrain, it merges them into a
single record under one name. The other resort then becomes unsearchable, and
the surviving record's piste km describes something larger than its name.
Verified example (Stage 0 QA, 2026-07-26): OpenSkiMap id
01ebf9136b08663b151ea8896e3ba66547ea5482 is named 'Alta Badia' and reports
252.8 km. Its own `places` localities are Abtei-Badia, Corvara, San Ciascian
(Alta Badia) AND Santa Cristina, Selva, Urtijei — the three villages of Val
Gardena — spanning IT-BZ and IT-BL. Two marketed resorts, one record.
WHAT WE DO AND DO NOT DO
We ADD ALIASES so the merged record is findable under either name, and attach
a boundaryNote the UI must display so the km figure is not read as one resort.
We DO NOT split the geometry or apportion the km between the two resorts. We
have no faithful basis for that split, and a guessed number presented as piste
km is exactly the kind of fabrication this project refuses to ship. Someone
choosing a week's holiday on '130 km vs 175 km' deserves a real number or an
honest 'these two are merged upstream'.
Aliases are also derived automatically from each area's `places` localities —
that is free and factual. This file is only for MARKETED names that appear in
no upstream field at all.

overrides.boundaryNote: OpenSkiMap merges Alta Badia and Val Gardena into a single lift-linked area. The piste total covers BOTH resorts, not Alta Badia alone. Verified 2026-07-26 from the record's own locality list.
overrides.source: derived from OpenSkiMap places localities + operator marketing names
operator marketing names; the Stage 0 QA report showed 'Madonna di Campiglio' matching nothing

_countryOverridesComment: Explicit country corrections, for the cases where upstream evidence is a
genuine tie and no automatic tie-break can resolve it.
The normalizer picks a primary country by frequency of valid `places`
entries, tie-broken by the first-stated regionCode. That works everywhere
except a true 1-1 split, where the tie-break just agrees with whichever
side upstream happened to list first. Overriding needs an external fact,
Only add a row here when the country is independently verifiable and you
have checked it. Record where you checked.

countryOverrides.evidence: Kaunertal Glacier is in Tyrol, Austria (Tiroler Oberland, Landeck district), reached by the 26 km Kaunertal Glacier Road from Feichten. Its published 3,108 m summit matches this record's topElevM of 3107, confirming it is the same place. Upstream splits 1-1 between IT and AT after inconsistent entries are dropped, and the regionCode tie-break lands on IT because IT-BZ is stated first. The centroid (46.865, 10.709) is on the Austrian side of the ridge.
countryOverrides.effect: Drops out of a GE/BG/IT build entirely, which is correct — it is an Austrian resort.
